description: Group content by user needs and propose routes, labels and internal relationships.
accomplishes: Group content by user needs and propose routes, labels and internal relationships. Preserve important existing URLs or plan explicit redirects. Explain navigation, breadcrumbs and content ownership. Validate findability before assuming a new structure is better.
prompt:
Act as a web developer.

Task: Define website information architecture.

Input context:
- AUDIENCES: [AUDIENCES]
- CONTENT INVENTORY: [CONTENT INVENTORY]
- PRIORITY TASKS: [PRIORITY TASKS]

Group content by user needs and propose routes, labels and internal relationships. Preserve important existing URLs or plan explicit redirects. Explain navigation, breadcrumbs and content ownership. Validate findability before assuming a new structure is better.

Preserve the existing architecture, minimise dependencies and define scope, acceptance criteria and relevant tests. Keep secrets server-side. No production changes or deployment without approval.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Service website map
Group offers under Services, evidence under Work and practical articles under Resources. Keep Contact available from the main navigation. Record existing URLs before proposing changes and avoid orphaning useful pages. Test whether a reader can locate service scope and the next action. No navigation experiment or redirect deployment is claimed.
